title: Readonly classes
summary: PHP 8.2 lets a whole class be declared readonly, so every declared property is readonly without repeating the modifier on each one.
new_code_policy: On a feature ceiling of 8.2 or above, when every property a class declares is (or will be) readonly, declare the class itself `readonly` instead of writing `readonly` on each property or promoted constructor parameter.
existing_code_policy: When every property on an existing class is already individually marked `readonly` and the class has no mutable property, collapsing to a class-level `readonly` modifier is a safe, purely cosmetic simplification. Do not apply it to a class that mixes readonly and mutable properties, or that relies on `#[AllowDynamicProperties]` or dynamic property creation, since a readonly class forbids both.
guideline: Prefer `final readonly class Foo { ... }` over repeating the `readonly` modifier on every property or promoted parameter once a class's properties are uniformly readonly.
details: PHP 8.2 added readonly classes (RFC readonly_classes): prefixing a class declaration with `readonly` marks every typed property it declares as readonly, and is only valid when all such properties can legally be readonly (no untyped or static properties). This is purely a declaration-site shorthand for what individually-marked readonly properties already expressed; it changes no runtime behavior. PHP 8.3 extended the same modifier to anonymous classes and, separately, allowed readonly properties to be reinitialized while cloning inside `__clone()` — both are expansions of the surrounding readonly-property feature, not changes to readonly classes themselves. PHP 8.4 narrowed that clone-time reinitialization behavior slightly. Neither PHP 8.4 nor PHP 8.5 UPGRADING mentions any deprecation or removal of readonly classes.
notes: PHP 8.3 allowed anonymous classes to be declared readonly and allowed readonly properties to be reinitialized during cloning inside __clone() — both extend the readonly-property feature rather than changing readonly classes as introduced in 8.2.
PHP 8.4 applied a narrow behavior tightening around that clone-time reinitialization. No PHP 8.2-8.5 UPGRADING file records a deprecation or removal of readonly classes.
